scenario: An oil-exploration company recruits seismic analysts who demonstrate strong subsurface geophysics knowledge OR advanced digital signal-processing skill. The specialisms are independent in the graduate pool; the OR-gate generates negative within-team correlation.

data.description: Population base rates and OR-gate selection mechanism

values.selection_rule: OR gate: selected if (subsurface geophysics knowledge) OR (digital signal-processing skill)

question: (a) Derive P(selected) from the OR-gate model. (b) Compute P(geophysics | ¬signal_processing, selected) and explain why it equals 1. (c) Compute P(geophysics | signal_processing, selected) and show it equals P(geophysics). (d) Quantify the induced conditional correlation direction and explain why it is a selection artefact rather than a genuine population relationship between subsurface geophysics knowledge and digital signal-processing skill.

ground_truth.explanation: Under OR-gate selection a candidate who lacks digital signal-processing skill must possess subsurface geophysics knowledge to be admitted — hence P(geophysics|¬signal_processing,sel)=1.0. A candidate who already has digital signal-processing skill is admitted regardless of subsurface geophysics knowledge, so P(geophysics|signal_processing,sel)=P(geophysics)=0.39. The gap (1.0 vs 0.39) creates a negative within-selected correlation that is purely a collider-selection artefact.

naive_answer: The negative correlation between subsurface geophysics knowledge and digital signal-processing skill observed among selected candidates reflects a genuine trade-off between these traits in the domain.
naive_trap: The negative correlation is entirely a Berkson collider artefact produced by the OR-gate admission rule; the two traits are independent in the full population.
reasoning_trace: (1) P(sel)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)=0.39+0.51-0.39×0.51=0.7011. (2) Among candidates without digital signal-processing skill: only those with subsurface geophysics knowledge are selected → P(geophysics|¬signal_processing,sel)=1.0. (3) Among candidates with digital signal-processing skill: selected regardless of subsurface geophysics knowledge → P(geophysics|signal_processing,sel)=P(geophysics)=0.39. (4) Within-selected: knowing ¬signal_processing raises P(geophysics) from 0.39 to 1.0 → negative conditional correlation despite population independence.
python_verification:
pA,pB = 0.39,0.51
pSel = pA+pB-pA*pB
assert abs(pSel-0.7011)<0.005, f'pSel={pSel}'
pA_notB_sel = pA*(1-pB)/(pA*(1-pB))   # =1.0 by definition
assert abs(pA_notB_sel-1.0)<1e-9
pA_B_sel = pA*pB/pB                    # =pA by definition
assert abs(pA_B_sel-0.39)<1e-9
assert pA_notB_sel > pA_B_sel, 'negative collider correlation confirmed'
